mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 4.5%) indicates accommodative monetary policy that reduces the risk-free rate, increasing the present value of equity cash flows and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS < 4.5%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate (UNRATE > 5.0%) indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, which signals reduced consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE > 5.0, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and real personal consumption (RSAFS) from the prior month indicates weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS decline, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 110, the economy enters a contraction phase, reducing corporate output and profit margins, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO < 110, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 4.5% (FEDFUNDS > 4.5%) indicates restrictive monetary policy, which increases the cost of capital and reduces equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.5, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A quarterly GDP growth rate above 0.5% (computed from GDPC1) indicates strong economic activity, which increases corporate earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when GDPC1 growth > 0.5%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and employment (PAYEMS) indicates a broad-based economic slowdown, which triggers negative equity returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when both INDPRO and PAYEMS decline, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in total non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) below 138,000 thousand indicates weakening labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when PAYEMS < 138000, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.
